title: Pages have their own vocabulary: words recur within their page more than chance
statement: In paragraph text, the share of certain words of four or more glyphs that were already written earlier on the same page is greater than when the words are dealt out at random across pages.
source: Registered as a target for generators after R-008 (a one-table line chain with nearby copying reproduced 7 of 8 facts). Public practice split: 0.311 against a mean of 0.223 for words shuffled across pages (Zandbergen-Landini), 0.307 (Takahashi), 0.294 (RF); training pages 0.291; it also holds on blocks of 40 training pages taken separately. No absolute threshold is set because the share grows with the length of a page. Generators on the practice split: the R-008 text gives 0.179 and the chain alone 0.190, both failing, since one table serves every page; a chain whose table drifts along the text (fitted on a moving window of public pages) gives 0.299 and passes. So this is not evidence of language: ordinary texts with page topics would pass too, and so does a meaning-free procedure whose tables change as it goes. It separates procedures with one fixed table from those with local tables.
